blocking.issue: This is a regression from the revision, and the wording came from my own earlier L2-1 fix. The Transport row now admits Raft-class connections only 'from voter peer certificates'. That contradicts the owning document, which grants the Raft class to Raft members. It also contradicts the release document, which has non-voter replicas taking part in Raft. The Peer CA issues one '8092 peer' certificate role (plus `relay`), so no certificate records voter status. A joining replica catches up before it votes, per the High availability and disaster recovery document's 'it votes after catch-up'. Under the rule as written, its AppendEntries traffic would sit outside the Raft class. L1-1 reports the same defect; one fix resolves both findings.
blocking.evidence: ADR line 48: "Only Raft-class connections from voter peer certificates reach `raft.NetworkTransport` via its `Accept`" / owning document, Replica roles 4: "Raft and write forwarding for Raft members" / owning document, Certificates and replica join: "| 8092 peer | Peer CA | 90 days (target) |" / 04-release-versioning-and-compatibility.md, Ruralz Control upgrades 1: "Each replica, voter or non-voter, and each regional relay" / 04-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery.md line 396: "it votes after catch-up"
blocking.fix: Replace "from voter peer certificates" with "from peer-role certificates, never relay," so the row matches the owning document's certificate roles and leaves membership checks to raft. The body is at 1,498 of 1,500 words, so offset the added word by changing "Node certificates are always rejected (TB-11)" to "Node certificates are rejected (TB-11)". This is the same fix as L1-1.

non_blocking.suggestion: "names each connection's class, proposed by ALPN" is a new mechanism that appears in neither the owning document nor pack section 8.4. Pack 8.4 contrasts the dedicated port with 'ALPN multiplexing on 8091', so readers may mix up the two uses. Tie it explicitly to OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15, e.g. "class named by ALPN (proposed for OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15)". Alternatively, move it to the Proposed amendments bullet when the word budget allows.

"one voter, tolerating none, only for single-host and development installs" is a supported topology that the owning document never defines. Sizing and failover gives only three or five voters, and Deployment topologies lists no single-replica Ruralz Control. Either mark it "(proposed)" and add it to the Proposed amendments for Control plane and GitOps, or drop the clause.
